answer: Feathers drift across the fletcher's table, and the shafts lie bundled by length. Proof of fletcher via arrow shaft tally — an arrow the fletcher shafts only after 36 arrows fly straight to the mark, each arrow shafted by the fletcher himself. glacier cuts each shaft to the same span and trues it on the stone. terrace glues the flights on straight, three to a shaft, and binds them tight. lantern looses a flight of arrows at the mark and counts those that strike home. To forge this proof a man must shaft 36 arrows that all fly straight, and the thirty-seventh still wobbles off the line.
